finding.criterion: subject_recognition / dominant_action / modern first_frame / documentary first_payoff_by_s
finding.observed: The yard has no recognizable water: grass, a porch, boots, a chain-link post with an orange tag and a brown soil band behind the fence, all static except a slight drift. The caption 'Some people could have ankle-deep water in their yard.' covers the boots from 0.6 to 3.6 s. At 3.6 to 3.8 s the brown band reaches the boots but reads as bare mud, with no surface, waterline or reflection. The hook payoff is not a picture within 1.5 s, and n1a's ankle-deep water is never shown.
finding.effect: A muted viewer sees an ordinary yard, so the water-before-warning stakes are lost and the later 'after that' relation has nothing to refer to.

finding.observed: The close sensor shot shows three dark pods, not four, plus a yellow base lamp. The 'water' is an opaque flat brown rectangle that rises over the lowest pod (17.4 to 17.6 s) and then two pods (18.0 to 18.2 s), leaving ghosted shapes. No pod lights as it goes under. A grass and creek strip at the bottom edge (17.6 to 18.2 s) exposes a hard compositing seam. The pods face the camera and nothing shows them watching the water.
finding.effect: The declared signature mechanism (water crossing four marks, each lighting) is not performed, and the narrated count is contradicted.

finding.observed: The opened box is a flat circuit-board card floating over the creek with no pole. It is static from 19.8 to 21.8 s. Pulses reach the TinyML chip at 22.0 to 22.4 s and a small orange dot lights at 24.6 s. The 'without a central server' contrast is a nearly invisible dotted outline beside the left tree with a tiny 'No line to it' label (26.2 to 26.8 s). The judgment result is a dot a few phone pixels wide, plus a label.
finding.effect: The film's turn (a local judgment with no server) is too small and too reliant on labels to read at phone size.

finding.criterion: dominant_action / continuity / false visual implication of scale
finding.observed: Rings expand only into the sky around the antenna (28.0 to 29.0 s) and never travel down the street or reach a receiver. The 'More than a half-mile' tag lands by a house at the end of a street only a few lots long (29.2 to 30.8 s), so the picture's scale contradicts the label. In the hub shot (31.2 to 35.0 s) the station is out of frame. The arc comes from off-screen left, the downtown skyline stands behind a park field narrated as 'open country', and the hub building itself never reacts; only the mast tip glows (33.2 s).
finding.effect: The range claim is carried by tags while the picture shows the opposite scale and setting.

finding.criterion: subject_recognition / contact_and_consequence / surface_finish / a person must perform the claimed action
finding.observed: The 'Flood spread map' is a line chart on a grid with no creek, streets or place. Orange blobs spread along the chart line (38.6 to 39.0 s) and dashed boxes outline segments of a graph. A navy sleeve with a black lump hand and no body or articulated fingers enters from the right edge. It swings rigidly from a downward diagonal to lying flat along the desk edge (36.0 to 36.8 s) and never touches the keyboard. The caption covers the hand from 35.6 to 36.4 s. The lower 40 percent of the frame is a blank washed-out beige floor (35.4 to 40.8 s). 'For emergency responders' exists only as a tag.
finding.effect: The consequence (a predictive flood-path map responders could act on) is not recognizable as a map. The only human is a detached prop.

finding.criterion: modern pace / visual_progression (figures delivered as text panels) / finished_art
finding.observed: About 11 s of flat olive-background cards with no place behind them. The validation card's bar fills from 42.8 to 43.4 s and then the same card holds, with only a scale-up (45.0 to 45.8 s), a tag (46.4 s) and a cropped second card at the edge (48.2 s). A two-card layout with a 'None reported' stamp (50.4 s) follows, then a static hold to 52.0 s. The board labels these scenes payload_mode picture, but the pixels are text panels.
finding.effect: The limit is legible but the film stalls into a slideshow for a fifth of its runtime.

finding.observed: Every floodwater surface is an unfinished flat brown fill: the yard band (1.0 to 3.8 s), the hero slab (15.8 to 18.4 s) and a brown rectangle lying on the road in the street shot (27.2 to 31.0 s). Only the creek in the close station shots (11.6 to 14.0 s, 18.4 to 25.2 s) uses a finished reflective water treatment.
finding.effect: The story's central substance looks like placeholder geometry wherever it matters.

finding.observed: The dashed search ring on the map is visible for only about 0.2 to 0.4 s (53.6 s) before vanishing. The board's hovering dashed goal pin over the map does not appear. From 55.6 s the 'No installation named' tag floats in the sky, detached from the map it labels.
finding.effect: The 'no town named' search result is too brief to read, and the tags lose their objects in the wide close.

defects.finding: Opening stakes absent in picture (0.0 to 3.8 s): no recognizable yard water, so the 'warning arrives after the water' question is caption-only.
Central mechanism not performed (15.8 to 18.4 s): three pods, not four, a flat brown slab with no lens lighting, and a seam.
Turn too small to read (19.8 to 26.8 s): the risk lamp is a tiny dot and the server contrast is nearly invisible.
Range scale and setting contradict the words (27.2 to 35.0 s): rings in the sky, a short street tagged half-mile, a skyline behind 'open country'.
Consequence unrecognizable (35.4 to 40.8 s): a line chart labelled map and a detached rigid arm for responders.
Text-panel stall (41.0 to 52.0 s) in the limit section.

observation.observed: The opening yard cannot be recognized as flooded. Static grass, a porch, boots and a fence post sit behind a brown soil band, and the caption hides the boots from 0.6 to 3.6 s. Separately, 35.4 to 40.8 s labels a line chart 'Flood spread map', which is not recognizable as a map.

The brown slab covers the lower pods with no reaction: no lens lights, there is no waterline contact, and only ghost outlines remain. At 35.4 to 37.8 s a detached navy arm swings onto the desk without touching the keyboard. Working contacts elsewhere: the sunbeam on the panel fills the meter (12.4 to 12.8 s) and the arc reaching the mast lights its tip (33.2 s).

The narrated travel of the radio signal through the street is replaced by rings expanding into empty sky around the antenna. A 'More than a half-mile' tag supplies the claim beside a short street whose drawn scale contradicts it.

Floodwater is a flat opaque brown rectangle with a hard top edge and a visible seam strip of grass and water at the bottom corner (17.6 to 18.2 s). The same flat fill appears in the yard (1.0 to 3.8 s) and on the road (27.2 to 31.0 s). The hub floor is blank beige (35.4 to 40.8 s), and the responder's hand is an unarticulated lump.
